MarijuanaNews still seems to be largely alone in reporting on the context for the declining fortunes of cannabis prohibition in Europe, so I think that it is again worth looking at -- and behind -- recent events there.

As reported Friday, the London police are going to stop arresting marijuana users in one section of London.
See
A Weird Week in the World of Marijuana Prohibition: Paranoid in Boise, Practical in London, And an Unusual Line-Up On the Supreme Court. Two Stories and Two Footnotes.

This innovation is being described as a pilot project that will be extended to all of London, if it is successful. Of course, if it is extended to all of London, then it will be impossible to justify arresting people in other parts of England and Wales. (Scotland has its own system, but it is likely to follow suit.) That will mean de facto decriminalization to an extent even beyond that of many other EU members, or what is currently contemplated by most Canadian politicians.
See
Leader of Canadian Tories Supports " Decriminalization " – Not " Legalization " -- Again. This Makes Mere " Decriminalization " a Defeat for Us. Defining Our Terms and Setting Our Goals.

Saturday, 30,000 people turned out in heavy rain to attend the Cannabis Freedom Festival in the Brixton area of south London, which is the area covered by this new policy. This kind of attendance in such bad weather gets noticed by politicians.

This means that the only logical next step is legalization, de facto, or de jure. The UK drug policy reform group Transform described it as " the beginning of the end for current drugs laws ". It is always possible that the Blair government will pull the plug on this test, but events in the Conservative Party make that increasingly unlikely.

The battle for the Tory leadership looks more and more like a rejection of social conservatism. The leading social conservative, shadow Home Secretary (justice minister) Ann Widdecombe, said that she would not seek the leadership, which she had zero chance of winning. It has not escaped anyone’s notice that the Conservative Party’s polling numbers never recovered from her advocacy of cracking down on cannabis users.
See
We Are Winning! Measuring the Progress Toward Legalization in the UK – 2 Articles
and links.

Indeed, the Independent On Sunday newspaper reported yesterday that " Widdecombe's moral authoritarianism serves to unite most Conservative MPs. They are, quite simply, united against her. " It went on to say that " No doubt, the party will have intense arguments about precise issues such as the legalisation of cannabis… "

The currently favored candidate for the Tory leadership is Michael Portillo, a social liberal, who has admitted to having a gay affair in his youth. Even more shocking is the fact that his father was openly Spanish, giving a whole new meaning to " throwing a Spaniard in the works. "

In an interview on the BBC, one Tory MP, Alan Duncan ­ a Portillo supporter ­ said the party should be all about " sex, drugs and rock'n'roll. " Now that should kill the rave movement!

The leader of the UK’s third largest party, the Liberal Democrats, has called for a Royal Commission on marijuana prohibition,
See
Leader of UK’s Third Largest Party Calls For Royal Commission On " Drugs " Policy,
Especially Marijuana, Gets Strong Support From Bishop Of Edinburgh.
Government Continues To Fear Truth and Freedom -- 4 Articles
so there is little for Blair to gain by continuing to oppose the will of the people, and that especially includes medical cannabis.

Consequently, another development reported by the Guardian on Saturday indicates what may be a de facto acceptance of medical cannabis by the UK, at least in London.

Excerpt:

Shop openly sells cannabis for medicinal use

Supplier claims police turn blind eye to drug dealing

By Sarah Hall
From the Guardian

June 16, 2001

The owner of a health food shop is openly selling cannabis for medicinal use in the heart of London's King's Cross with the apparent approval of local police, the Guardian can reveal.

Tony Taylor, of Tony's Hemp Corner, has around 250 customers, including doctors and lawyers. He claims local police, who arrested him on charges of growing and supplying the plant three years ago, turn a blind eye to his practice as they concentrate on tackling the area's prostitutes and crack cocaine dealers.

Mr Taylor, who was given an absolute discharge after his arrest three years ago, yesterday described the attitude of police in London's red-light district to his business as " really cool ".

" The council and the police know exactly what's going on and the police think what I'm doing is really good, " he said from his office, where he keeps accounts and copies of the GP letters he requires.

" They come around sometimes and say, 'How are you doing, are there any problems?' We've obviously been granted grace because there are so many other problems in King's Cross. "

However, Islington police last night denied they knew about Mr Taylor's medicinal cannabis dealing. " We weren't aware that he was prescribing drugs for patients with GPs' letters, " said Detective Chief Inspector Robin Hopes. " We'd like to get around a table with him and work out if what he's doing is legal or illegal. "

Mr Taylor, who offers cannabis at less than the street price, refuses to supply it for recreational use and clients have to fill in a form, undergo a 20-minute interview and provide him with a GP's letter.

And it gets even worse for the prohibitionists in events that seemingly had nothing to do with cannabis policies.

George Bush’s European trip was successful, indeed it was another triumph of lowered expectations. The European elite and media had painted such a negative picture of him that anything short of drooling would have been positive. However, it was the prohibitionist Swedes who ended up looking bad.

Last week’s EU Summit in Gothenburg was a major embarrassment for the Swedes, who had already given up on making an issue of their moral superiority on " drugs " – their national obsession. Prohibition is failing so badly that they decided not to talk about it.
See
Swedish Prohibitionism Disintegrating. 2 Articles

Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson, who also holds the rotating EU Presidency for six months, was the most anti-American of the European leaders, telling demonstrators that the EU was " one of the few institutions we can develop as a balance to U.S. world domination.'' He even quoted Lenin! How not to win American friends.
See
Drug Bizarro Continues Lying In Sweden; Attacks Dutch Again

As a comic aside, demonstrating how completely out of touch with reality the prohibitionist media are, consider this jewel from Reuters:
" Swedes reacted with stunned dismay to Friday's orgy of destruction, which overwhelmed the libertarian country's police force, barred by law from using tear gas and water cannon in riot control. "

Sweden, where the police can arrest you and compel you to take a blood test if they just think that you may have used " drugs ", is a " libertarian country? " Actually, they are a schizophrenic country with paranoid delusions about " drugs. "
See
Two Press Releases from Swedish Prohibitionists Tell Us A Little About Dutch and Australian Policies – And Too Much About the Prohibitionist Mentality.

On the other hand, the summit was something of an unexpected success for the Dutch.

The Radio Netherlands web site survey of the Dutch newspapers reports that the popular Amsterdam paper, De Volkskrant " runs an item on the Dutch prime minister, Wim Kok, which should put a smile on his face. The paper says that, according to diplomats both Dutch and foreign, Mr Kok ‘is able to work as a binding element between the Schröders, the Blairs, and the Chiracs. He never makes anyone angry, and he's always searching for a compromise. He's the one who comes up with the formulation that satisfies everyone ". The paper notes that it was Mr Kok - and not Mr Schröder or Mr Chirac - who wasseated next to US president George W Bush during dinner, giving him an opportunity for ‘all kinds of little bilateral chats’. The paper says that the diplomatic community seems to be quite interested in what Mr Kok's next move will be. It says speculation in Brussels is that he'll run for another term as prime minister, but that he'll leave after two years to take on a ‘top international position’ ".

This is not all about small talk, either. The Dutch have just agreed to let DEAland use their bases in the Netherlands Antilles for flights over Colombia. Thus, they, not the prohibitionist, anti-American, Lenin quoting Swedes, are our real friends. All of this makes a difference. If the Dutch want to amend or " denounce " the UN anti-drug treaties because of their cannabis policies, is DEAland going to be in a position to object? Less and less so, every day.
See
We Are Winning! The Dutch Government Shows More Confidence that Things Are Going Our Way in Europe.

Marijuana prohibition does not exist in a geopolitical vacuum. Washington surely recognizes that they have lost Europe on this, just as they are losing Canada – and the American people.

This week saw several developments that put us further on the road to freedom.
